pick.headline: Todor Zhivkov ousted in Bulgaria
pick.summary: On 10 November 1989 the Bulgarian Communist Party removed Todor Zhivkov, its leader since 1954, replacing him with Foreign Minister Petur Mladenov.
pick.significance: Zhivkov had been the longest-serving leader in the Soviet bloc; his fall, the day after the Berlin Wall opened, showed the collapse spreading across Eastern Europe.
pick.fbis: Albanian radio, citing BTA, reported on 11 November that Zhivkov had resigned his highest party and state posts at a Bulgarian Central Committee plenum held the day before.
